scope: Directed, non-exhaustive review of ten studies on publication maps, disciplinary structure, bibliometric relatedness or topic evolution. Counts describe these studies, not community-wide prevalence.
counting_rule: One occurrence per study and model family used in a relevant analysis. Do not count bibliography mentions, software wrappers, model ancestry, different versions of one paper, or models used only in a separate general retrieval benchmark.

studies.title: An appraisal of publication embedding techniques in the context of conventional bibliometric relatedness measures
studies.evidence: Institutional record and abstract explicitly identify the four representations compared; full PDF fetch failed. Exact BERT and SciBERT checkpoints/pooling not confirmed.
studies.note: Word2Vec here embeds citation labels, not the same textual input. DOI qss_a_00168 belongs to a different paper.

studies.title: The landscape of biomedical research
studies.evidence: Full publisher JATS obtained in the prior review and read again locally, including pilot methods and exact model list.
studies.note: PubMedBERT is used for the full map; all eight encoders appear in the pilot comparison. Do not call all eight final-map models.

studies.title: Representing the disciplinary structure of physics: a comparative evaluation of graph and text embedding methods
studies.note: MPNet is the paraphrase variant, not all-mpnet-base-v2. SciBERT uses a sum of the last four CLS states.

studies.title: A framework for demonstrating, forecasting, and explaining topic evolution by analyzing geometrical motion of topic embeddings
studies.evidence: Publisher-indexed methods/results and author code vec_by_bert.py and vec_by_mpnet.py. Direct full publisher fetch failed; code read, never executed.
studies.note: Studies topic evolution using topic/context representations associated with papers, not an identical whole-paper mapping protocol.

studies.title: Density, asymmetry and citation dynamics in scientific literature
studies.evidence: Full author text, Document embeddings section and maps in figure 6.
studies.note: SBERT checkpoint not identified in the text read: no attribution to MPNet/MiniLM. SPECTER is explicitly not used.

studies.title: Citation importance-aware document representation learning for large-scale science mapping
studies.evidence: Full author PDF, sections 4.1.2, 4.2 and 4.3; publication title and DOI confirmed via Crossref.
studies.note: Count only the four pretrained encoders explicitly compared in the PubMed science-mapping task. The other models belong to the separate SciDocs evaluation; some baseline results are taken from other publications.

studies.title: The Knowledge Cosmos: An Immersive Platform for Interdisciplinary Research Discovery
studies.evidence: Full author PDF downloaded and parsed, Methods section. Author PDF has an earlier title: A Playful, Immersive Platform for Exploring Science.
studies.note: Uses approximately 17 million precomputed SPECTER embeddings. SciBERT explains their ancestry, not a separate model run.

studies.title: Identifying interdisciplinary emergence in the science of science: combination of network analysis and BERTopic
studies.evidence: Full publisher HTML retrieved and read, methods text specifying the default representation actually used.
studies.note: MPNet is mentioned as a comparison of speed/quality from elsewhere, not run in this study. BERTopic is the pipeline, not another embedding model.

studies.title: An Efficient Deep Learning Framework for Revealing the Evolution of Characterization Methods in Nanoscience
studies.evidence: Full JATS retrieved via Europe PMC, body confirmed by paper-lookup parser, methods/results read.
studies.note: Maps topics and their evolution in a specific research domain.

studies.title: Use of diverse data sources to control which topics emerge in a science map
studies.venue: MetaROR open peer review / arXiv author manuscript
studies.evidence: Full MetaROR HTML retrieved; text-similarity methods specify allenai-specter. Version 2 page evaluates arXiv v3 and links a v4 title revision.
studies.note: Count once across versions. Calls its similarity network BERT, but the actual model is SPECTER. Distinct from Bascur et al. 2025 Which topics..., which used BM25.
